newsitem.title: USA: Dean Witter, Morgan Stanley to merge.
newsitem.headline: Dean Witter, Morgan Stanley to merge.

text.p: Morgan Stanley Group Inc. and Dean Witter, Discover & Co. Wednesday announced the biggest merger ever in the securities industry, a $10.7 billion deal that promised to reshape the landscape on Wall Street.

The merger would combine Dean Witter's retail brokerage and Morgan Stanley's investment banking business into a powerhouse with $271 billion in assets under management, the largest among U.S. securities firms, the companies said.

The merged company would present a serious challenge to Merrill Lynch & Co. Inc., which had been the only Wall Street firm with a major presence in the areas of mergers and acquisitions and stock and bond underwriting, as well as having an army of retail brokers.
Analysts said the merger could spawn a wave of copycat deals in which companies try to combine investment banking and retail brokerage operations.

"Nothing is outside the realm of possibility," said Lawrence Rice, chief investment officer at Josephthal, Lyon & Ross. "You've got banks, insurance companies and even other brokerages all looking to make deals."

It is that kind of clout that led the white-shoe firm of Morgan Stanley, which typically caters to big investors, to merge with Dean Witter, whose brokers once worked out of Sears Roebuck stores and typically deal with smaller, retail investors.

"The combination of Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter, Discover may be as close to an ideal merger as there is," said Dean Witter Chairman Philip Purcell, who will be chairman of the new company, Morgan Stanley, Dean Witter, Discover & Co.
Analysts also said the merger was a good fit.
"This is synergistic. You can see savings flowing both ways," George Salem at Gerard Klauer Mattison said after a presentation by Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley executives.

At the presentation, executives stressed how Dean Witter's retail brokers could sell Morgan Stanley's mutual fund and other products while Dean Witter's card business could become a launch pad for an array of financial services.
Dean Witter has 361 branches with about 9,000 brokers. Its Discover credit card, with 39 million customers, is the nation's third-largest, measured by balances outstanding.

Morgan Stanley, formed in 1935, has 38 offices in 19 countries and has been a powerhouse in underwriting securities for corporations and governments and providing advice on mergers, acquisitions and other transactions.

While the companies said they will have more assets under management than any other firm, Merrill Lynch still had higher revenues, $13.1 billion in 1996, compared with $12 billion in combined 1996 revenues for Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter.

Morgan Stanley Chairman Richard Fisher said revenue growth, "extraordinarily diversified earnings" and the opportunity to use capital more efficiently were the main factors driving the planned merger, which was approved Tuesday by the boards of both New York-based companies.
"There are some consolidation savings," he told a news conference, "but they are not the reason for doing this."

The companies did not say if jobs would be cut, but officials noted there was little overlap between the two businesses, which could prove to be a major challenge as the two different corporate cultures are merged.
Investors welcomed the deal, sending Morgan Stanley's stock soaring $7.875 to $65.25 and Dean Witter's up $2 to $40.625, both in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The deal marks a turnaround for Dean Witter brokers, in particular, many of whom sold stocks in Sears stores in the 1980s before the retailer spun off the brokerage in 1993. Sears had acquired Dean Witter's predecessor, Dean Witter Reynolds, in 1981.
The deal also lifted the stocks of other Wall Street firms as investors bet more deals would follow.

Merrill rose $1.125 to $86.50, Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette added 87.5 cents to $38.50 and smaller, highly profitable retail brokers rose even more sharply, with A.G. Edwards Inc. up $1.875 to $36.375 and Alex. Brown Inc. up $2.125 to $54.625, all on the NYSE.
But shares of Painewebber Group, which had been rumoured as a target for Morgan Stanley, fell $2.75 to $36.125.

Under the merger pact, Dean Witter will swap 1.65 shares for each Morgan Stanley share, giving Dean Witter shareholders 55 percent and Morgan Stanley holders 45 percent of the new firm. Based on Dean Witter's stock price and Morgan Stanley's 158.9 million shares, the deal is worth more than $10.65 billion.
The merger needs approval by regulators and shareholders and is expected to be completed by mid-year, the firms said. The stock swap is designed to be tax free to shareholders.

John Mack, president of Morgan Stanley, will be president and chief operating officer of the merged company. Morgan Stanley's Fisher will be chairman of the executive committee of the new 14-member board, with seven from each company.
In connection with the deal, the firms granted each other options to acquire 19.9 percent of the other firm, a move typical in mergers meant to dissuade competing bids.
